title: KCET 2017 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA Final Answer Key - Chemistry (master key; no per-version columns, version code not printed on this copy)

questions.q: If $3.01 \times 10^{20}$ molecules are removed from 98 mg of H$_2$SO$_4$, then number of moles of H$_2$SO$_4$ left are
questions.explanation: Moles of H$_2$SO$_4$ initially = 98 mg / 98 g mol$^{-1}$ = $1\times10^{-3}$ mol = $6.022\times10^{20}$ molecules; removing $3.01\times10^{20}$ molecules leaves $3.012\times10^{20}$ molecules = $0.5\times10^{-3}$ mol.

questions.q: The correct set of quantum number for the unpaired electrons of chlorine atom is
questions.explanation: Cl has configuration [Ne]3s$^2$3p$^5$; its unpaired electron lies in a 3p orbital, so n=3, l=1, m=+1 (or -1), s=$\pm\dfrac{1}{2}$, matching option C.

questions.q: The electronegativities of C, N, Si and P are in the order of
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group, giving Si < P < C < N.

questions.q: Which of the following structure of a molecule is expected to have three bond pairs and one lone pair of electrons ?
questions.explanation: An sp$^3$-hybridised central atom with 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (as in NH$_3$) adopts a pyramidal shape.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct electron dot structure of N$_2$O molecule ?
options: N=N=O, with two lone pairs on the terminal N and two lone pairs on O, no formal charges
N≡N⁺–O⁻, triple bond between the two N atoms, positive charge on the central N and negative charge with three lone pairs on O
N=N=O, with only one lone pair shown on the terminal N (incomplete octet) and two lone pairs on O
N–N=O, single bond between the two N atoms with one lone pair on the terminal N, double bond to O with two lone pairs
questions.explanation: N$_2$O is best represented by resonance structures with formal charges; as per the KEA key both option B ($:N\equiv N^+-O^-:$) and option C are accepted. Chemically, the two standard resonance contributors are usually A and B, so this question is somewhat ambiguous (as per KEA key).

questions.q: The pressure of real gases is less than that of ideal gas because of
options: Increase in the number of collisions
Increase in the kinetic energy of the molecules
questions.explanation: Attractive forces between real gas molecules reduce the force and frequency of collisions with the container walls, lowering the observed pressure compared to an ideal gas.

questions.q: A reaction has both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ – ve. The rate of reaction
options: remains unaffected by change in temperature
cannot be predicted for change in temperature
questions.explanation: With $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ both negative, $\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S$ becomes more negative (more favourable) as temperature decreases, so the reaction (and its effective rate of product formation) is favoured at lower temperature.

questions.q: The equilibrium constant for the reaction N$_{2(g)}$ + O$_{2(g)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NO$_{(g)}$ is $4\times10^{-4}$ at 2000 K. In presence of a catalyst the equilibrium is attained ten times faster. Therefore the equilibrium constant in presence of catalyst at 2000 K is
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up attainment of equilibrium but does not change the equilibrium constant, so K$_c$ stays $4\times10^{-4}$.

questions.q: The reaction quotient 'Q$_c$' is useful in predicting the direction of the reaction. Which of the following is incorrect ?
options: If Q$_c$ > K$_c$, the reverse reaction is favoured
If Q$_c$ < K$_c$, the forward reaction is favoured
If Q$_c$ = K$_c$, no reaction occurs
If Q$_c$ > K$_c$, forward reaction is favoured
questions.explanation: When Q$_c$ > K$_c$ the system shifts in the reverse direction, not forward, to reach equilibrium, so statement D is incorrect.

questions.q: 3ClO$^-_{(aq)}$ → ClO$^-$ + 2Cl$^-$ is an example of
questions.note: The equation as printed is likely a mis-transcription of 3ClO$^-\to$ClO$_3^-$+2Cl$^-$ (chlorine goes from +1 to +5 and to $-1$), which is a textbook disproportionation reaction, not a simple reduction; the KEA key nonetheless credits 'Reduction reaction', which is kept here as the official answer.
questions.explanation: The intended reaction is a disproportionation of ClO$^-$ (some Cl is oxidised to ClO$_3^-$, some reduced to Cl$^-$), but the KEA key marks this as a reduction reaction.

questions.q: In the manufacture of hydrogen from water gas (CO + H$_2$), which of the following is correct statement ?
options: CO is oxidized to CO$_2$ with steam in the presence of a catalyst followed by absorption of CO$_2$ in alkali.
CO and H$_2$ are separated based on difference in their densities.
H$_2$ is removed by occlusion with pd.
questions.explanation: In the Bosch process, CO in water gas is catalytically oxidised to CO$_2$ with steam, and the CO$_2$ formed is scrubbed out by absorption in alkali, leaving pure H$_2$.

questions.q: Plaster of Paris is represented as
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO$_4\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}$H$_2$O.

questions.q: Addition of mineral acid to an aqueous solution of Borax, the following compound is formed
questions.explanation: Borax (Na$_2$B$_4$O$_7\cdot$10H$_2$O) reacts with mineral acids to give orthoboric acid, B(OH)$_3$.

questions.q: Identify the correct statement in the following :
options: n-butane and isobutane are functional isomers
Dimethyl ether and ethanol are chain isomers
Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol are position isomers
Ethanoic acid and methyl methanoate are position isomers
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol share the same carbon chain and functional group but differ only in the position of the -OH group, making them position isomers.

questions.q: In which of the following, homolytic bond fission takes place ?
options: Addition of HBr to double bond
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Free-radical halogenation proceeds via homolytic cleavage of the Cl$_2$ bond to generate chlorine radicals, unlike the other options which involve heterolytic/ionic mechanisms.

questions.q: For the preparation of Alkanes, aqueous solution of sodium or potassium salt of carboxylic acid is subjected to
questions.explanation: In Kolbe's electrolytic method, electrolysis of the aqueous sodium/potassium salt of a carboxylic acid produces an alkane at the anode.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a common component of photo-chemical smog ?
questions.explanation: Photochemical smog consists mainly of ozone, acrolein, PAN and nitrogen oxides; CFCs are inert compounds associated with ozone-layer depletion, not smog.

questions.q:
Which of the following crystal has unit cell such that $a 
e b 
e c$ and $\alpha 
e  eta 
e \gamma 
e 90^\circ$ ?
questions.explanation: These unit-cell parameters describe the triclinic crystal system, which is exhibited by K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$.

questions.q: The correct statement regarding defect in solids is
options: Frenkel defect is usually favoured by a very small difference in the sizes of cations and anions.
Frenkel defect is a dislocation defect.
Trapping of proton in the lattice leads to the formation of F-centers.
Schottky defect has no effect on the physical properties of solids.
questions.explanation: In a Frenkel defect an ion moves from its lattice site to an interstitial site, so it is also known as a dislocation defect.

questions.q: In a face centred cubic arrangement of A and B atoms in which 'A' atoms are at the corners of the unit cell and 'B' atoms are at the face centers. One of the 'A' atom is missing from one corner in unit cell. The simplest formula of compound is
questions.explanation: Normally corner A atoms contribute $8\times\dfrac{1}{8}=1$ and face-centred B atoms contribute $6\times\dfrac{1}{2}=3$ per unit cell (AB$_3$); with one corner A missing, A contributes $\dfrac{7}{8}$, giving the ratio A:B = $\dfrac{7}{8}:3=7:24$, i.e. A$_7$B$_{24}$.

questions.q: Which of the following aqueous solution has highest freezing point ?
questions.explanation: Freezing-point depression is proportional to $i \times m$; NH$_4$Cl gives the fewest ions ($i=2$) among the given 0.1 molal solutions, so it has the smallest depression and hence the highest freezing point.

questions.q: The Vant Hoff's factor 'i' accounts for
questions.explanation: The Van't Hoff factor i = (actual number of particles)/(number of formula units), which measures the extent of dissociation (or association) of the solute.

questions.q: When the pure solvent diffuses out of the solution through the semi-permeable membrane then the process is called
questions.explanation: Normal osmosis moves solvent into the solution; forcing solvent out of a solution through a semipermeable membrane (against the natural gradient) is reverse osmosis.

questions.q:
The standard reduction potential at 298 K for the following half cell reactions

Zn$^{2+}_{(aq)}$ + 2e $\rightarrow$ Zn$_{(s)}$  E$^\circ$ = – 0.762 V

Cr$^{3+}_{(aq)}$ + 3e $\rightarrow$ Cr$_{(s)}$  E$^\circ$ = 0.740 V

2H$^+_{(aq)}$ + 2e $\rightarrow$ H$_{2(g)}$  E$^\circ$ = 0.0 V

F$_{2(g)}$ + 2e $\rightarrow$ 2F$^-_{(aq)}$  E$^\circ$ = 2.87 V

Which of the following is strongest reducing agent ?
questions.explanation: The species with the most negative standard reduction potential is oxidised most easily; Zn (E$^\circ$=–0.762 V) is therefore the strongest reducing agent among those listed.

questions.q:
By passing electric current, NaClO$_3$ is converted into NaClO$_4$ according to the following equation

NaClO$_3$ + H$_2$O $\rightarrow$ NaClO$_4$ + H$_2$

How many moles of NaClO$_4$ will be formed when three Faradays of charge is passed through NaClO$_3$ ?
questions.explanation: Converting ClO$_3^-$ to ClO$_4^-$ involves loss of 2 electrons per ion (Cl: +5 → +7); 3 F ÷ 2 F/mol = 1.5 mol of NaClO$_4$.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride solution, which of the half cell reaction will occur at anode ?
questions.explanation: Despite the lower theoretical oxidation potential requirement for water, Cl$^-$ is preferentially oxidised at the anode due to overpotential effects, releasing Cl$_2$ gas — the basis of the chlor-alkali process.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is in accordance with the Arrhenius equation ?
options: Rate of a reaction increases with increase in temperature
Rate of a reaction increases with decrease in activation energy
Rate constant decreases exponentially with increase in temperature
Rate of reaction does not change with increase in activation energy
questions.explanation: By the Arrhenius equation $k=Ae^{-E_a/RT}$, the rate constant (and hence rate) increases both with increasing temperature and with decreasing activation energy, so statements A and B are both correct.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is incorrect ?
options: The rate law for any reaction cannot be determined experimentally
Biomolecular reactions involve simultaneous collision between two species
Molecularity is only applicable for elementary reaction.
questions.explanation: Rate laws are in fact determined experimentally (e.g. by the method of initial rates), so statement A is the incorrect one.

questions.q: For a reaction $\dfrac{1}{2}$A $\rightarrow$ 2B rate of disappearance of A is related to rate of appearance of B by the expression
questions.explanation: For $\dfrac{1}{2}$A$\to$2B, rate $=-\dfrac{1}{1/2}\dfrac{d[A]}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[B]}{dt}$, which simplifies to $-\dfrac{d[A]}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{4}\dfrac{d[B]}{dt}$.

questions.q: The process which is responsible for the formation of delta at a place where rivers meets the sea is
questions.explanation: River-borne colloidal clay particles coagulate on meeting the electrolytes present in seawater, depositing as a delta.

questions.q: Hydrogenation of vegetable oils in presence of finely divided Nickel as catalyst. The reaction is
questions.explanation: The solid Ni catalyst and the liquid/gaseous reactants are in different phases, making this heterogeneous catalysis.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a favourable condition for physical adsorption ?
questions.explanation: Physical adsorption is exothermic and favoured by low temperature; high temperature disfavours it.

questions.q: The metal extracted by leaching with a cyanide is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Silver is extracted from its ore by leaching with cyanide solution (Mac Arthur–Forrest process).

questions.q: Extraction of chlorine from brine solution is based on
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Chlorine is liberated from brine by oxidation of Cl$^-$ ions at the anode (Cl$^-\to\dfrac{1}{2}$Cl$_2$+e$^-$) during electrolysis.

questions.q: Which of the following element forms p$_\pi$-p$_\pi$ bond with itself ?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen's small atomic size allows effective sideways overlap of 2p orbitals, forming strong p$_\pi$-p$_\pi$ bonds (as in N$\equiv$N); heavier elements like P, Se and Te have larger, more diffuse p orbitals that overlap poorly.

questions.q: Which one of the following metallic oxide exhibit amphoteric nature ?
questions.explanation: Al$_2$O$_3$ reacts with both acids and bases, showing amphoteric character, unlike the basic oxides CaO, Na$_2$O and BaO.

questions.q: Select wrong chemical reaction among the following :
questions.explanation: Cl$_2$ with dilute NaOH actually gives NaCl and NaOCl (or NaClO$_3$ with hot concentrated NaOH), not H$_2$ and O$_2$, so equation C is incorrect.

questions.q: Which one of the following noble gas has an unusual property of diffusing through the materials such as rubber, glass or plastic ?
questions.explanation: Helium's very small atomic size lets it diffuse through materials like rubber, glass and plastic unusually easily.

questions.q: The magnetic nature of elements depends on the presence of unpaired electrons. Identify the configuration of transition elements which shows highest magnetic moment ?
questions.explanation: 3d$^5$ (e.g. Mn$^{2+}$) has the maximum possible number of unpaired electrons (5) among the given configurations, giving the highest magnetic moment.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is wrong regarding Lanthanoids ?
options: Ln(III) compounds are predominantly ionic in character.
The ionic size of Ln(III) ions decreases with increasing atomic number.
Ln(III) hydroxides are mainly basic in nature.
questions.explanation: Most Ln(III) ions have partially filled 4f orbitals and show colour due to f–f transitions, so 'generally colourless' is the wrong statement.

questions.q: Square planar complex of the type MAXBL (where A, B, X and L are unidentate ligands) shows following set of isomers
questions.explanation: A square planar M(A)(X)(B)(L) complex with four different unidentate ligands exists as three geometrical isomers; per the KEA key these are described as two cis and one trans arrangement.

questions.q: According to crystal field theory, the M – L bond in a complex is
questions.explanation: Crystal field theory treats the metal–ligand interaction as a purely electrostatic (ionic) attraction between the metal cation and the ligands.

questions.q: The co-ordination number and the oxidation state of the element 'M' in the complex [M(en)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)]NO$_2$ {where (en) is ethan-1,2-diamine} are respectively
questions.explanation: Two bidentate en ligands (4 donor sites) plus one bidentate oxalate (2 donor sites) give coordination number 6; with NO$_2^-$ as the counter ion the complex ion is +1, so M + 0 − 2 = +1, giving M = +3.

questions.q: Toluene reacts with halogen in presence of Iron (III) chloride giving ortho and para halo compounds. The reaction is
questions.explanation: FeCl$_3$ generates an electrophile that substitutes a ring hydrogen of toluene — a classic electrophilic aromatic substitution.

questions.q:
In the following sequence of reactions

CH$_3$Br $\xrightarrow{KCN}$ A $\xrightarrow{H_3O^+}$ B $\xrightarrow{LiAlH_4}$ C

The end product C is
questions.explanation: CH$_3$Br + KCN → CH$_3$CN (A); H$_3$O$^+$ hydrolysis of the nitrile gives CH$_3$COOH (B); LiAlH$_4$ reduction of the acid gives CH$_3$CH$_2$OH (C), i.e. ethyl alcohol.

questions.q: Which of the following order is true regarding the acidic nature of phenol ?
questions.explanation: The electron-donating methyl group in o-cresol decreases acidity relative to phenol, while the electron-withdrawing nitro group in o-nitrophenol increases it, giving O-cresol < phenol < O-nitrophenol.

questions.q: Which of the following reagent cannot be used to oxidize primary alcohols to aldehydes ?
options: Heating in presence of Cu at 573 K
questions.explanation: Acidic KMnO$_4$ is a strong oxidiser that over-oxidises primary alcohols all the way to carboxylic acids, so it cannot be used to isolate the aldehyde.

questions.q: Cannizzaro's reaction is an example of auto oxidation
options: It is a typical reaction of aliphatic aldehyde.
It is a reaction answered only by aromatic aldehydes.
It is a reaction answered by all aldehydes.
It is a reaction answered by only aldehydes containing α -hydrogen.
questions.explanation: Cannizzaro's (self oxidation-reduction) reaction is given by aldehydes lacking an α-hydrogen, typically aromatic aldehydes (and HCHO); since none of the options states this precisely, KEA awarded grace marks to all candidates (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Lower members of aliphatic carboxylic acid are soluble in water. This is due to
options: Formation of hydrogen bonds with water.
Van der-Waals interaction with water molecules.
questions.explanation: Lower aliphatic carboxylic acids form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, which makes them water-soluble.

questions.q: The correct order of increasing basic nature for the bases NH$_3$, CH$_3$NH$_2$ and (CH$_3$)$_2$NH in aqueous solutions
questions.explanation: Considering electron density together with solvation/steric effects in water, the taught base-strength order is NH$_3$ < CH$_3$NH$_2$ < (CH$_3$)$_2$NH.

questions.q:
The product formed during the following reaction are

CH$_3$–C(CH$_3$)$_2$–O–CH$_3$ + HI → ?  [(CH$_3$)$_3$C–O–CH$_3$, i.e. tert-butyl methyl ether, reacting with HI]
questions.explanation: HI cleaves tert-butyl methyl ether by an SN1 mechanism at the more stable tertiary carbon, giving (CH$_3$)$_3$C–I and CH$_3$OH.

questions.q: Reduction of ketones cannot be carried out with which of the following reagents ?
options: Sodium borohydride or Lithium Aluminium hydride
Hydrazine and KOH in ethylene glycol
Hydrogen in presence of palladium in Barium sulphate and quinoline
questions.explanation: H$_2$/Pd–BaSO$_4$/quinoline (Lindlar's catalyst) selectively reduces alkynes to alkenes and does not reduce the carbonyl group of ketones.

questions.q: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used in the preparation of primary amine from phthalimide, which of the following reagent is not used during the process ?
questions.explanation: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis uses KOH (to deprotonate phthalimide), an alkyl halide (for N-alkylation) and NaOH/hydrazine hydrolysis to release the primary amine; HCl plays no role in the sequence.

questions.q: The Glycosidic linkage present in sucrose is between
options: C-1 of α-glucose and C-2 of β-fructose
C-1 of α-glucose and C-4 of α-glucose
C-1 of β-galactose and C-4 of α-glucose
C-1 of α-glucose and C-4 of β-fructose
questions.explanation: Sucrose is formed by a glycosidic bond between C1 of α-glucose and C2 of β-fructose.

questions.q: Hormones are secreted by ductless glands of human body. Iodine containing hormone is
questions.explanation: Thyroxine, secreted by the thyroid gland, is the iodine-containing hormone among the options.

questions.q: Pick the wrong statement from the following :
options: Sources of Vitamin B$_1$ are yeast, milk, green vegetables and cereals
Deficiency of Vitamin B$_6$ (pyridoxime) results in convulsions
Consumption of citrus fruits and green leafy vegetables in food prevents scurvy
Deficiency of vitamin D causes xerophthalmia
questions.explanation: Xerophthalmia results from vitamin A deficiency, not vitamin D (whose deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia), so statement D is wrong.

questions.q: The monomer used in Novolac, a polymer used in paints
questions.explanation: Novolac, used in paints, is formed by the acid-catalysed condensation of phenol and formaldehyde.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a biodegradable polymer ?
options: Polyhydroxy butyrate – CO – β hydroxy valerate
questions.explanation: PHBV, poly-3-hydroxybutyrate-co-β-hydroxyvalerate and Nylon-2-Nylon-6 are designed to be biodegradable; Glyptal/Glyptol is a non-biodegradable thermosetting polymer.

questions.q: Bactericidal antibiotics among the following is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Ofloxacin (a fluoroquinolone) is bactericidal, whereas erythromycin, tetracycline and chloramphenicol are bacteriostatic.

questions.q: Pick the correct statement among the following :
options: Cetyl trimethyl ammonium bromide is a popular cationic detergent used in air conditioner
Non-ionic detergents is formed when polyethylene glycol reacts with adipic acid
Sodium dodecyl benzene sulphonate used in tooth paste is a cationic detergent.
Sodium lauryl sulphate forms an insoluble scum with hard water.
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Cetyl trimethyl ammonium bromide is indeed a popular cationic detergent used in hair conditioners; the printed option says 'air conditioner', likely a typographical error for 'hair conditioner', so KEA awarded grace marks to all candidates (as per KEA key).
